statement: For a centered finite Gaussian vector X with covariance C, finite nonnegative nonzero coefficient vectors a_p, xi,beta>0, let f_p=log sum_i a_pi exp(xi X_i), w_pi=a_pi exp(xi X_i)/exp(f_p), pi_p=exp(-beta f_p)/sum_q exp(-beta f_q), bar_w=sum_p pi_p w_p, A=sum_p pi_p[sum_i C_ii w_pi-w_p^T C w_p], and B=sum_p pi_p w_p^T C w_p-bar_w^T C bar_w. Then d/dxi E[-log sum_p exp(-beta f_p)/beta]=xi E[A-beta B], B>=0, and 0<=A<=max_i C_ii.
assumptions: X centered Gaussian; C positive semidefinite
Finitely many coefficient vectors, nonnegative and each nonzero
xi,beta>0
proof_or_counterexample: ATTEMPT.md L1 gives differentiated Gibbs weights, full-covariance Gaussian integration by parts and the exact pair-variance decomposition.
remaining_gap: No uniform regularization-scale information or exact LQG exponent follows from L1.

statement: Under L1 with positive definite C and distinct coefficient vectors, the minimum of f_p is unique almost surely for each fixed xi>0. With p_* the minimizer, A_*=sum_i C_ii w_{p_*i}-w_{p_*}^T C w_{p_*}, S=lim_beta beta E B exists, is finite and nonnegative, and (E min_p f_p)'=xi(E A_*-S)<=xi max_i C_ii.
assumptions: L1 assumptions
C positive definite
Duplicate coefficient vectors removed
Fixed xi>0; beta limit taken before any scale limit
proof_or_counterexample: ATTEMPT.md L2 proves uniqueness by nonzero analytic zero sets and passes the finite-beta identity with dominated first derivatives; it does not discard beta B.
remaining_gap: The beta limit is at fixed finite model; no beta/cutoff exchange has been proved.

statement: For two parallel edges of base length one and independent standard normal X_1,X_2, F=log min(exp(xi X_1),exp(xi X_2))=xi min(X_1,X_2). Its expected xi derivative is -1/sqrt(pi), the within-path covariance term is zero, and the switching term is S=1/(xi sqrt(pi)). Omitting switching therefore has absolute derivative error 1/sqrt(pi).
assumptions: xi>0
Two independent standard normal costs and two single-edge candidate paths
proof_or_counterexample: ATTEMPT.md L3 evaluates E|X_1-X_2| exactly. measurements.json independently reproduces the finite-beta approach to this exact limit.
remaining_gap: Toy graph does not determine the GFF crossing exponent.

statement: For the finite Gaussian minimum log length F of L2 and V=max_i C_ii, Var(F)<=xi^2 V and every median M satisfies |E F-M|<=xi sqrt(2V). For heat-smoothed whole-plane GFF crossings with T=log(1/epsilon), V=T+O(1), and the established median exponent, sufficiently accurate finite polygonal/quadrature approximants F_n have E F_n/T_n -> xi Q(xi)-1 at every fixed xi in a compact interior parameter interval.
assumptions: Finite Gaussian gradient bound and Gaussian Poincare inequality
For the LQG extension: smooth regularized GFF with finite L2 supremum, diagonal variance T+O(1), and cited median exponent
Finite approximants have uniform-in-xi L2 error <=1/n; tiny auxiliary noise makes their covariances positive definite
proof_or_counterexample: ATTEMPT.md L4 proves the median bound and an existential finite-path/quadrature approximation, avoiding an unproved fixed-direction lattice identification.
remaining_gap: Uses the published median exponent; it does not evaluate Q(xi). The approximation is existential, not a uniform computational algorithm.

statement: For the approximants in L4, define g_n=E F_n/T_n, Psi_n=(V_n/T_n)xi^2/2-g_n and dmu_n=[xi/T_n][V_n-E A_{n,*}+S_n]dxi. These are nonnegative measures converging weakly on compact interior intervals to dmu=d[xi^2/2-(xi Q(xi)-1)]. From xi_*=1/sqrt(6) and g(xi_*)=-1/6, for xi>xi_* one has g(xi)=-1/6+(xi^2-1/6)/2-mu((xi_*,xi]); for xi<xi_* the corresponding interval mass has the opposite orientation. Computing mu determines Q but mu is not computed here.
assumptions: L1-L4
Continuity of cited Q and the Brownian anchor
V_n/T_n ->1
No absolute continuity or differentiated scale limit is assumed

remaining_gap: H: no explicit mass of the limiting measure, no absolute continuity, and no exact generic d_gamma. Record as reduction only.

statement: For two candidate paths at a fixed xi>0 in L1, set Delta=f_1-f_2 and D=(w_1-w_2)^T C(w_1-w_2). If the weighted gap measure nu(E)=E[D 1_{Delta in E}] has a density continuous at zero on a neighborhood of zero, then lim_beta beta E B_beta equals that density at zero.
assumptions: L1 with two paths
xi fixed positive
Weighted gap density exists near zero and is continuous at zero
No independence between Delta and D
